government.title: Corruption Perceptions, the Pendleton Act, and Sovereign Borrowing Costs
government.short_title: Corruption Perceptions, the Pendleton Act, and Sovereign Borrowing Costs
government.plain_summary: This study looked at how the Pendleton Act, a law that aimed to reduce corruption in government hiring, affected the government's ability to borrow money. If the Act was effective in stopping corruption, it would mean the government could borrow money at a better rate. The research found that after the Pendleton Act was passed, the government paid about 63 to 84 fewer cents for each dollar borrowed. This means the Act worked as intended and helped the government save money by borrowing at a lower interest rate.

government.short_title: Bridging the Physical–Institutional Gap: Spatiotemporal Evolution of Three-Dimensional Urbaniz…
government.source: Journal of Urban Planning and Development
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how shrinking cities in China are managing their physical space and institutional resources. It found that while the balance between these two areas is improving, it's still uneven across different regions. The research used a model to show how political, development, and governance factors work together differently in various places. This helps us understand how to better manage shrinking cities by tailoring solutions to specific areas, which can lead to more effective urban planning and resource allocation.

government.title: The Legal Foundations for the Evolving Role of Oversight Bodies in Combating Corruption in Iraq
government.short_title: The Legal Foundations for the Evolving Role of Oversight Bodies in Combating Corruption in Iraq
government.source: Interdisciplinary Studies in Society, Law, and Politics
government.plain_summary: This research looks at how the legal system in Iraq supports oversight bodies in fighting corruption. It examines the laws and constitution that give these bodies their powers and how they've grown stronger over time. The study also looks at international agreements that have influenced Iraq's approach. The main goal is to make sure these bodies can effectively monitor and prevent corruption.

government.short_title: Evaluation of the Policymaking System and Institutions for Combating Administrative Corruption…
government.source: Journal of Historical Research, Law and Policy
government.plain_summary: During the Republican period in Afghanistan (2004-2021), administrative corruption was a major issue affecting governance. The government worked with international support to create laws, anti-corruption strategies, and institutions. However, despite progress in these areas, corruption did not significantly decrease. The study found that while there were improvements in legislation and institution building, the effectiveness of policies weakened at implementation stages.

government.title: Evaluation of Iran's Legislative Criminal Policy on the Smuggling of Goods and Currency via Official Channels: A Critical Analysis of the 2013 Anti‑Smuggling Law and Its 2021 Amendments
government.short_title: Evaluation of Iran's Legislative Criminal Policy on the Smuggling of Goods and Currency via Of…
government.source: Journal of Historical Research, Law and Policy
government.plain_summary: The smuggling of goods and currency through official channels in Iran remains a significant issue despite various laws enacted over the years. While there have been efforts like the 2013 Anti-Smuggling Law and subsequent amendments, this practice has not decreased but may have worsened in some areas such as reverse smuggling and organized currency trafficking. This article examines how well these laws balance different goals like prevention, repression, rehabilitation, and compensation. It found that while there are positive changes, the law still faces major issues including a broad definition of smuggling, multiple bodies leading to lengthy proceedings, disproportionate penalties, and weak enforcement due to corruption.

government.title: Prevention of Conflicts of Interest in Integrated Territorial Development in Moscow: Implementation of CSTO Anti-Corruption Standards in Urban Planning Zoning
government.short_title: Prevention of Conflicts of Interest in Integrated Territorial Development in Moscow: Implement…
government.plain_summary: This article talks about how to prevent corruption in Moscow's urban planning. It identifies risks like changing land use and giving out plots to developers, which can lead to corruption. The author suggests a four-level system to stop this from happening. This system helps ensure that projects are done fairly and without favoritism.

government.title: THE CYBERNETIC DIAGNOSTIC OF ANTI-NARCOTIC SYSTEM: MODEL RAS-VI AS A TOOL OF SYSTEMIC EVALUATION
government.short_title: THE CYBERNETIC DIAGNOSTIC OF ANTI-NARCOTIC SYSTEM: MODEL RAS-VI AS A TOOL OF SYSTEMIC EVALUATI…
government.source: Problems of Social Hygiene, Public Health and History of Medicine
government.plain_summary: The study proposes a cybernetic diagnostic tool called RAS-VI (Resilience-Adaptability-Synergy-Diversity Index) for evaluating the effectiveness of anti-narcotics policies at different levels. This model uses principles from cybernetics and systems theory to assess how well regional anti-narcotics systems can adapt, work together, and maintain stability. Key indicators like resilience, adaptability, synergy, and diversity are used to measure these aspects. By applying RAS-VI, policymakers can better understand the strengths and weaknesses of their system and improve its overall effectiveness in managing drug issues.

government.title: The treasury single account and fiscal transparency and accountability in federal universities of Nigeria
government.short_title: The treasury single account and fiscal transparency and accountability in federal universities…
government.plain_summary: The Treasury Single Account (TSA) was implemented in 2015 to centralize public funds and improve transparency and accountability in Nigerian federal universities, but financial irregularities still occur. This study found that TSA has improved transparency and accountability significantly (p=0.004), but also faces challenges like bureaucratic delays and actors circumventing the system. Corruption persists as it transforms into less traceable forms. Despite savings of over 10 trillion Naira nationally, corruption perception scores remain low.

government.title: AI Regulation and Its Social Impacts on Public Policy
government.short_title: AI Regulation and Its Social Impacts on Public Policy
government.plain_summary: AI is now a key part of how governments make decisions in many areas like healthcare, policing, and welfare. As more AI systems are used, it's important to have rules to make sure they work fairly and don't cause problems. These rules help ensure that AI doesn't lead to unfair treatment or less democracy. By carefully watching how AI is used, we can make sure it helps people and doesn't hurt them.

government.title: Le facteur émotionnel de l’activité : analyser les « angles morts » pour améliorer la QVCT. Bilan d’une recherche immersive en Police Judiciaire française
government.short_title: Le facteur émotionnel de l’activité : analyser les « angles morts » pour améliorer la QVCT. Bi…
government.plain_summary: This research focuses on understanding the emotional risks in police work and how they manage their emotions to improve job satisfaction. It was conducted by observing various police units like forensic science, digital investigation, financial division, criminal division, anti-terrorism unit, and more over 26 days. The study found two key emotions that are hard for them to express: interest and frustration. These emotions make it difficult for officers to discuss their work-related feelings openly, leading to invisible or undiscussed labor.

government.title: A Policy Analysis of PFAS Regulations in Maine and the US Federal Government
government.short_title: A Policy Analysis of PFAS Regulations in Maine and the US Federal Government
government.plain_summary: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are harmful chemicals found in many products that have contaminated the environment. The US government has not uniformly addressed PFAS issues, but some states like Maine have taken strong actions. Maine has implemented various measures such as education, labeling requirements, and bans on certain agricultural practices. They also have unique regulations like banning the use of PFAS in food products like beef, dairy, and eggs.

government.title: Data Science as a Catalyst for Audit Transformation
government.short_title: Data Science as a Catalyst for Audit Transformation
government.plain_summary: Data science has become crucial as we generate vast amounts of information daily. It helps transform this data into useful insights for better decision-making across various sectors. For audit institutions, integrating data science can enhance their ability to manage public funds more effectively and improve accountability. By using data science, audits can provide clearer and more accurate reports that recommend improvements faster, which benefits the overall administration and improves citizens' quality of life.

government.title: Killer Robots – A Case for SAIs
government.short_title: Killer Robots – A Case for SAIs
government.plain_summary: This paper discusses a scenario where autonomous killer robots are used in warfare without human intervention. These robots can make decisions about who to target based on AI algorithms trained to recognize certain uniforms. If one of these drones targets and kills an enemy soldier who is surrendering, it would violate international laws. Another concern is if the robot makes a mistake by attacking another similar system, leading to unintended conflicts.

government.title: The dark side of public service motivation : Analysis of noble cause corruption based on the Lebanese case
government.short_title: The dark side of public service motivation : Analysis of noble cause corruption based on the L…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how public service motivation can lead to noble cause corruption in Lebanon, where there's a lot of social and economic hardship. The research found that feelings like compassion and selflessness often push people into doing good deeds for noble causes, but these actions sometimes involve corrupt practices. This leads to internal conflicts as the person feels both guilty and supported by their work environment. Factors like physical exchanges, personal space in the workplace, and close relationships with users can make it easier for this type of corruption to happen.

government.title: La face sombre de la motivation de service public : Analyse de la corruption pour une cause noble à partir du cas libanais
government.short_title: La face sombre de la motivation de service public : Analyse de la corruption pour une cause no…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how public service motivation can lead to corruption for a noble cause in Lebanon, where corruption is prevalent and social issues are challenging. Based on interviews with 32 Lebanese public servants, the research explores how feelings of compassion and self-sacrifice related to public service motivation might encourage them to engage in corrupt behavior for what they see as a good cause. The study highlights that these motivations can lead to behaviors like providing extra support or shielding users from punishment. This can create internal conflicts within the public servant due to their emotional connection with those affected.

government.title: The economic impact of public corruption Heilongjiang in China
government.short_title: The economic impact of public corruption Heilongjiang in China
government.source: Annals of Public and Cooperative Economics
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how corruption in Heilongjiang province in China affected the economy. In 2004, a big corruption scandal led to a province-wide anti-corruption effort. The analysis shows that after this event, the province saw a decline in economic activities like GDP, investment, and exports. At the same time, the government increased spending.

government.title: Corruption in health systems: An umbrella review of the pathways to health, financial, and social outcomes
government.short_title: Corruption in health systems: An umbrella review of the pathways to health, financial, and soc…
government.plain_summary: Corruption in health systems can significantly impact health, financial, and social outcomes. This review found that common types of corruption include substandard medicines, informal payments, absenteeism, and billing abuse. These issues can lead to avoidable deaths and economic strain, especially in low-resource settings. Corruption also disproportionately affects poorer and rural populations, leading to mistrust and widening health inequities.

government.title: The Impact of Forensic Auditing, The Code of Ethics for Indonesian Accountants, and the Public Accountant Law on the Elimination of Corruption at PT PLN
government.short_title: The Impact of Forensic Auditing, The Code of Ethics for Indonesian Accountants, and the Public…
government.source: Journal of Economics, Finance And Management Studies
government.plain_summary: This study looked at how forensic auditing, the Code of Ethics for Indonesian Accountants, and the Public Accountant Law help reduce corruption at PT PLN. The research found that these measures work together to make sure that the company operates more honestly. Practitioners can use this information to understand how these legal and ethical frameworks can prevent corruption in their own work. By following these guidelines, they can ensure their organizations are more transparent and accountable.

government.title: Algorithmic Management in Australian Workplaces: A Study on Transparency, Accountability and Worker Protection in AI-Driven Employment Decisions
government.short_title: Algorithmic Management in Australian Workplaces: A Study on Transparency, Accountability and W…
government.source: Lecture Notes in Education Psychology and Public Media
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how AI is used in workplaces in Australia, particularly in hiring, performance reviews, pay, and promotions. While AI can help make decisions faster, the current laws don't fully protect workers. The laws are mostly reactive, meaning workers can only get help after they've been unfairly treated. The study suggests adding more steps before AI makes decisions, like letting workers know what the AI is doing and why, having a human review the AI's decisions, and making sure the AI isn't used to make all decisions.

government.title: Local Government Politics and Governance: Local Government Governance Innovation in Realizing Responsive Public Services
government.short_title: Local Government Politics and Governance: Local Government Governance Innovation in Realizing…
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how local governments can improve their services to better meet the needs of their communities. It identifies several ways local governments are innovating, such as using digital tools, combining services from different departments, and listening to community feedback. These innovations help make services more responsive and accessible. However, there are challenges like uneven access to technology and bureaucratic resistance.

government.title: State‐Controlled Fact‐Checking During COVID‐19: A Case of Thailand's Anti‐Fake News Center
government.short_title: State‐Controlled Fact‐Checking During COVID‐19: A Case of Thailand's Anti‐Fake News Center
government.plain_summary: Fact-checking is a common response to fake news, especially in authoritarian countries like Thailand. The Anti-Fake News Center (AFNC), a state-controlled fact-checking organization, often performs more repressive functions rather than genuinely verifying false information. Instead of ensuring accurate information, AFNC helps the government monitor critics and control the spread of information, which can be used to suppress dissent and promote state narratives. This practice shows how authoritarian regimes use fact-checking to control information and maintain power.

government.title: The infectious disease burden in kidney transplant recipients: a 20-year multicenter cohort study on non-graft-failure hospitalizations in eastern China
government.short_title: The infectious disease burden in kidney transplant recipients: a 20-year multicenter cohort st…
government.plain_summary: This study looked at hospital stays for kidney transplant recipients over 20 years in eastern China. It found that infections were the main reason for these stays, with pneumonia and urinary tract infections being common. About one in five transplant recipients had at least one non-graft-related hospital stay. The study also showed that infections led to most deaths among transplant recipients.

government.title: Editorial: Managing competing demands in contemporary public sector accounting: tensions between innovation, accountability, sustainability and public value
government.short_title: Editorial: Managing competing demands in contemporary public sector accounting: tensions betwe…

government.title: Governing Through Values: Pangngadereng Service Ethics, Accountability, Transparency, and Citizen Trust in Makassar, Indonesia
government.short_title: Governing Through Values: Pangngadereng Service Ethics, Accountability, Transparency, and Citi…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how service ethics based on local values in Makassar, Indonesia, influence citizen trust. It found that service ethics, accountability, and transparency are interconnected, with service ethics having a strong influence on both accountability and transparency. The study used a validated instrument to measure these values and found that service ethics strongly predicted accountability and transparency, which in turn predicted trust. The research provides a practical tool for local governments to monitor interaction quality.

government.title: Corruption as a Governance Challenge in Kenya. A Case of Meru County
government.short_title: Corruption as a Governance Challenge in Kenya. A Case of Meru County
government.source: Journal of Public Policy and Governance
government.plain_summary: Corruption is a significant issue in Kenya, especially in devolved units like Meru County. This study found that nepotism and favoritism in hiring are the most common forms of corruption, with 71% of respondents agreeing. Misuse of public funds and embezzlement of county resources are also prevalent. The study recommends measures such as competitive recruitment processes, transparent expenditure reporting, and publishing tender awards to increase public scrutiny and reduce corruption.

government.title: Institutional readiness for business process integration in Tanzania’s public sector: a TOE-based analysis
government.short_title: Institutional readiness for business process integration in Tanzania’s public sector: a TOE-ba…
government.source: Transforming Government: People, Process and Policy
government.plain_summary: This study looked at how ready Tanzania's public sector is for better connecting its different government departments and services. They found that strong support from government leaders and clear plans are very important. Also, having good technology like computers and internet is crucial. But the biggest challenge is having enough money to keep these systems running and improving them.

government.title: When drugs speak: an exploratory convergent mixed-methods study of a first-person creative narrative activity for anti-seizure medication pharmacology in undergraduate medical education
government.short_title: When drugs speak: an exploratory convergent mixed-methods study of a first-person creative nar…
government.plain_summary: This study evaluated a creative writing activity called "When Drugs Speak" for teaching anti-seizure medications to medical students. The activity involved students writing from the perspective of an anti-seizure medication, giving it a personality and story based on its pharmacological properties. Over 90% of students preferred this activity over traditional revision methods and reported improved retention and interest in pharmacology. The writing showed students engaged with various aspects of pharmacology, though less so with pharmacokinetic information.

government.title: Algorithmic Authority in Practice: Generative AI, Decision-Making, and Accountability in Public Administration
government.short_title: Algorithmic Authority in Practice: Generative AI, Decision-Making, and Accountability in Publi…
government.plain_summary: This study explores how generative AI (GenAI) is changing how public officials make decisions and hold each other accountable. It found that GenAI can concentrate decision-making authority in officials who don't understand it, leading to some decisions being automatically accepted and others overridden. GenAI's outputs can also make officials feel less accountable, as responsibility is spread out. The study suggests that while GenAI can improve performance, it can also make it harder for officials to maintain trust with the public.

government.title: Government Transparency Increases Trust in Government: Disentangling Effects of Government Transparency From Effects of Information
government.short_title: Government Transparency Increases Trust in Government: Disentangling Effects of Government Tra…
government.plain_summary: The study found that government transparency generally increases trust in government, but this relationship can be explained by different theories. Government transparency can make people trust the government more, which aligns with the idea that government acts help citizens understand and participate in decision-making (deliberative democracy theory). However, it also shows that the information disclosed can either increase or decrease trust, depending on how the information is presented. This means that when the government discloses information, it can either build or break trust, not just because of the transparency itself but also because of the information provided.

government.title: Governing artificial intelligence in public services: accountability, transparency and democratic AI governance
government.short_title: Governing artificial intelligence in public services: accountability, transparency and democra…
government.source: Transforming Government: People, Process and Policy
government.plain_summary: This paper discusses how democratic governments can manage artificial intelligence in public services by creating frameworks that are transparent, accountable, and governable. It proposes a framework called TAG, which stands for Transparent, Accountable, and Governable. The TAG Framework combines elements like transparency, accountability, and governance to ensure AI is used ethically and responsibly. Practically, this means things like public registers of AI systems, assessing the impact of algorithms, having human oversight, and regular audits.

government.title: From Soft-Law AI Ethics to Risk-Based Public Sector AI Procurement: Recalibrating Malaysia’s Post-PDPA Governance Model
government.short_title: From Soft-Law AI Ethics to Risk-Based Public Sector AI Procurement: Recalibrating Malaysia’s P…
government.source: LAW & PASS: International Journal of Law, Public Administration and Social Studies
government.plain_summary: In recent years, governments have started acquiring AI systems through procurement rather than developing them in-house. This change means that instead of just ensuring ethical principles are followed, governments need to make those principles enforceable throughout the AI system's lifecycle. In Malaysia, they have introduced guidelines for AI governance and procurement. However, simply having privacy compliance and ethical principles isn't enough to manage AI in public administration.

government.title: Whistleblowing Policy and Anti-Corruption Effort in Nigeria's Public Sector, 2015-2024
government.short_title: Whistleblowing Policy and Anti-Corruption Effort in Nigeria's Public Sector, 2015-2024
government.source: JOURNAL OF PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION AND SOCIAL WELFARE RESEARCH
government.plain_summary: This study looked at how Nigeria's public sector handles whistleblowing and anti-corruption efforts from 2015 to 2024. It found that while the policy helped recover some public funds, it faced many challenges like weak laws, lack of protection for whistleblowers, and poor coordination among agencies. Many whistleblowers faced retaliation, which discouraged them from coming forward. The study suggests making stronger laws, improving how agencies work together, and educating the public more to make the policy more effective.

government.title: Network Governance for Sustainable Development: Enhancing Partnerships to Implement UN SDGs in Anti‐Desertification Projects
government.short_title: Network Governance for Sustainable Development: Enhancing Partnerships to Implement UN SDGs in…
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how different groups can work together more effectively to fight desertification and restore land, which is part of the United Nations' Sustainable Development Goals. It found that simply telling people what to do isn't as effective as involving everyone and thinking about how systems work together. By doing this, they can get more people involved and keep working together even when things get complicated. This is important for countries trying to improve their environment and meet these goals.

government.title: The Wheel of Corruption as a Vehicle for Development? Global Debates, African Realities, And a Reappraisal of the Abacha Loot
government.short_title: The Wheel of Corruption as a Vehicle for Development? Global Debates, African Realities, And a…
government.source: JOURNAL OF PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION AND SOCIAL WELFARE RESEARCH
government.plain_summary: The debate on corruption as a development tool has been revived in global discussions. Some argue that illicit wealth can be used for development if properly managed. This article looks at this idea from a global and African perspective, focusing on Nigeria's Abacha-loot case. It found that while recovering assets can bring some benefits, corruption often leads to new forms of rent-seeking.

government.title: The Impact of Poor Records Management Practices on Service Delivery and Accountability in Local Government Councils (LGCs) in Oyo State, Nigeria
government.short_title: The Impact of Poor Records Management Practices on Service Delivery and Accountability in Loca…
government.source: JOURNAL OF PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION AND SOCIAL WELFARE RESEARCH
government.plain_summary: This study found that local government councils in Oyo State, Nigeria often use outdated paper-based systems for managing records. This leads to delays in service delivery and increased fees for expedited services. It also makes it harder to track who is responsible for what, which can lead to misuse of power. To improve, councils need to digitize their records, train staff on modern record management, and strengthen accountability measures.

government.title: Treasury Single Account (TSA), Accountability and Transparency in Public Finance Management in Nigeria
government.short_title: Treasury Single Account (TSA), Accountability and Transparency in Public Finance Management in…
government.source: JOURNAL OF PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION AND SOCIAL WELFARE RESEARCH
government.plain_summary: The Treasury Single Account (TSA) has improved accountability and transparency in managing public finance in Nigeria, according to a study. The research found that TSA significantly affects how well public finance is handled. This means TSA is working well in ensuring that public money is used properly and openly. The study suggests that the government should continue to provide training for those who use TSA to make sure it works effectively.

government.title: Accountability and Good Governance in Local Government Administration: A Study of Obio/Akpor, Andoni, and Ahoada West in Rivers State, 2014–2024
government.short_title: Accountability and Good Governance in Local Government Administration: A Study of Obio/Akpor,…
government.source: JOURNAL OF PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION AND SOCIAL WELFARE RESEARCH
government.plain_summary: This study looked at how well local governments in three areas of Rivers State, Nigeria, are doing in terms of being accountable and providing good services. It found that when governments effectively manage resources, include everyone in decision-making, have regular public meetings, and improve health services, they are doing a good job. However, problems like weak structures, corruption, and interference from higher levels of government can hurt their performance. The study suggests ways to improve accountability and inclusiveness, like making budgets transparent, involving citizens more, and working together with other institutions.

government.title: Muslim Students Trust in Government Institutions: The Role of Religiosity, Administrative Transparency, and Public Service Quality in a Muslim-Majority Context
government.short_title: Muslim Students Trust in Government Institutions: The Role of Religiosity, Administrative Tran…
government.source: Journal of Government and Civil Society
government.plain_summary: Public trust in government institutions is crucial for effective governance, especially among educated youth in Muslim-majority societies. This study found that university students' trust in government is influenced by factors like religiosity, administrative transparency, and service quality. The research showed that service quality has the most significant impact on students' trust, more so than transparency or religious values. The study suggests that improving service quality is the most effective strategy for building trust in government institutions among young people.

government.title: From research to education to policy: Building a global field of sport ethics and integrity
government.short_title: From research to education to policy: Building a global field of sport ethics and integrity
government.plain_summary: This article discusses how a Master's program and a Doctoral program are creating a global field of sport ethics and integrity. The program uses research to develop educational materials and professional development programs. It also supports policy development by providing a strong evidence base. Through international collaboration, these programs have created a network of over 70 countries, and they support 17 doctoral researchers looking at integrity issues in sports from different perspectives.

government.title: Citizen Trust and Digital Governance Transformation: Ethical Challenges and Artificial Intelligence Governance in the Public Sector
government.short_title: Citizen Trust and Digital Governance Transformation: Ethical Challenges and Artificial Intelli…
government.source: Journal of Government and Civil Society
government.plain_summary: This study explores how public trust in AI-driven government services is growing, focusing on ethical considerations, explainable AI, and digital government transformation. It shows a rise in academic publications about these topics, indicating increasing interest in making AI more transparent and accountable. Key countries like the US, Germany, the UK, the Netherlands, and China are major contributors to this research. The findings highlight the importance of making AI understandable, ensuring ethical governance, and promoting transparency to build trust with citizens.

government.title: Corruption Network in Bank BJB Advertising Procurement: An NVivo Content Analysis
government.short_title: Corruption Network in Bank BJB Advertising Procurement: An NVivo Content Analysis
government.source: Journal of Government and Civil Society
government.plain_summary: This study examines corruption in the Bank BJB advertising procurement case, analyzing eight news reports from different media sources. The findings show that corruption was sustained through patronage, mutual benefit relationships, brokers, and informal networks. These practices led to financial losses for the state, policy distortions, reduced oversight, and declining accountability. The study highlights how actor configurations and relational mechanisms support organized corruption, offering insights for improving transparency and governance in public procurement.

government.title: Ethical Foundations of Anti-Corruption in the Civil Service System of the People’s Republic of China
government.short_title: Ethical Foundations of Anti-Corruption in the Civil Service System of the People’s Republic of…
government.plain_summary: This summary explains the ethical foundations of anti-corruption in China's civil service system. Unlike many countries that rely solely on formal laws, China uses a combination of official virtue shaped by Confucian tradition and socialist ideology. This approach balances party discipline with legal responsibility. The Chinese model shows how ethical principles are integrated into a system that includes traditional values, ideology, and centralized control.

government.title: STRENGTHENING GOVERNANCE INTEGRITY THROUGH E-PARTICIPATION: THE ROLE OF TRANSPARENCY AND RESPONSIVENESS IN MALAYSIAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT
government.short_title: STRENGTHENING GOVERNANCE INTEGRITY THROUGH E-PARTICIPATION: THE ROLE OF TRANSPARENCY AND RESPO…
government.source: International Journal of Law Government and Communication
government.plain_summary: This study highlights the importance of e-participation in enhancing the integrity of governance, particularly in local government in Malaysia. E-participation, which involves using digital tools for citizen-government interaction, can improve transparency and responsiveness. However, for e-participation to be effective, there needs to be institutional commitment and the ability to act on public input. The study shows that e-participation is more than just a communication tool; it's a form of governance that relies on the willingness of local authorities to respond to public needs.

government.title: How digital portfolios become governable: a venture design research study of public sector digital development
government.short_title: How digital portfolios become governable: a venture design research study of public sector dig…
government.source: Transforming Government: People, Process and Policy
government.plain_summary: This study explores how public sector organizations can better govern digital development projects. It suggests that instead of relying on existing tools, digital solutions should be designed to make governance more visible, comparable, and subject to collective decision-making. The research found that by actively specifying governance through design, digital solutions can lead to more transparent discussions and decisions. However, long-term outcomes like strategic alignment and public value creation are harder to measure.

nonprofit.title: Restructuring Accountability Through Participatory Grantmaking: Towards a Dialogic Approach
nonprofit.short_title: Restructuring Accountability Through Participatory Grantmaking: Towards a Dialogic Approach
nonprofit.plain_summary: Traditional grantmaking often leads to power imbalances where organizations with more resources make decisions that can sometimes ignore the needs of the communities they aim to help. Participatory grantmaking tries to change this by giving more decision-making power to the communities themselves. Our research shows that by doing this, it creates new ways of sharing power and responsibility. It also helps to prevent conflicts between the community's decisions and the rules set by bigger organizations.

nonprofit.title: From Reporting to Regulation: The Making and Governance of Financial Resilience Through the Charity Statement of Recommended Practice in England and Wales
nonprofit.short_title: From Reporting to Regulation: The Making and Governance of Financial Resilience Through the Ch…
nonprofit.plain_summary: This study looks at how charities in England and Wales developed a new accounting standard called SORP. Before this, charities didn't have a clear way to report their finances. The new standard was created to help charities be more transparent and accountable, especially after some scandals in the 1980s. By making financial reporting standardized, charities became easier to understand and manage, which helped regulators oversee them better.

nonprofit.title: THE CYBERNETIC DIAGNOSTIC OF ANTI-NARCOTIC SYSTEM: MODEL RAS-VI AS A TOOL OF SYSTEMIC EVALUATION
nonprofit.short_title: THE CYBERNETIC DIAGNOSTIC OF ANTI-NARCOTIC SYSTEM: MODEL RAS-VI AS A TOOL OF SYSTEMIC EVALUATI…
nonprofit.source: Problems of Social Hygiene, Public Health and History of Medicine
nonprofit.plain_summary: The study proposes a cybernetic diagnostic tool called RAS-VI (Resilience-Adaptability-Synergy-Diversity Index) for evaluating the effectiveness of anti-narcotics policies at different levels. This model uses principles from cybernetics and systems theory to assess how well regional anti-narcotics systems can adapt, work together, and maintain stability. Key indicators like resilience, adaptability, synergy, and diversity are used to measure these aspects. By applying RAS-VI, policymakers can better understand the strengths and weaknesses of their system and improve its overall effectiveness in managing drug issues.

nonprofit.title: Constitutional Diversity of Anti-Corruption Provisions and International Legal Standards
nonprofit.short_title: Constitutional Diversity of Anti-Corruption Provisions and International Legal Standards
nonprofit.source: INTERNATIONAL CRIMINAL LAW AND INTERNATIONAL JUSTICE
nonprofit.plain_summary: This article looks at how different countries' constitutions handle anti-corruption laws. It finds that most constitutions have similar ways of dealing with corruption, which can help create better anti-corruption rules. By understanding these common practices, we can make stronger anti-corruption laws that work for everyone. This is important because constitutions are like the highest rules in a country, and they help set up the system to fight corruption.

nonprofit.title: Local Government Politics and Governance: Local Government Governance Innovation in Realizing Responsive Public Services
nonprofit.short_title: Local Government Politics and Governance: Local Government Governance Innovation in Realizing…
nonprofit.plain_summary: This study looks at how local governments can improve their services to better meet the needs of their communities. It identifies several ways local governments are innovating, such as using digital tools, combining services from different departments, and listening to community feedback. These innovations help make services more responsive and accessible. However, there are challenges like uneven access to technology and bureaucratic resistance.

nonprofit.title: Institutional readiness for business process integration in Tanzania’s public sector: a TOE-based analysis
nonprofit.short_title: Institutional readiness for business process integration in Tanzania’s public sector: a TOE-ba…
nonprofit.source: Transforming Government: People, Process and Policy
nonprofit.plain_summary: This study looked at how ready Tanzania's public sector is for better connecting its different government departments and services. They found that strong support from government leaders and clear plans are very important. Also, having good technology like computers and internet is crucial. But the biggest challenge is having enough money to keep these systems running and improving them.

nonprofit.title: Whistleblowing Policy and Anti-Corruption Effort in Nigeria's Public Sector, 2015-2024
nonprofit.short_title: Whistleblowing Policy and Anti-Corruption Effort in Nigeria's Public Sector, 2015-2024
nonprofit.source: JOURNAL OF PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION AND SOCIAL WELFARE RESEARCH
nonprofit.plain_summary: This study looked at how Nigeria's public sector handles whistleblowing and anti-corruption efforts from 2015 to 2024. It found that while the policy helped recover some public funds, it faced many challenges like weak laws, lack of protection for whistleblowers, and poor coordination among agencies. Many whistleblowers faced retaliation, which discouraged them from coming forward. The study suggests making stronger laws, improving how agencies work together, and educating the public more to make the policy more effective.

nonprofit.title: Muslim Students Trust in Government Institutions: The Role of Religiosity, Administrative Transparency, and Public Service Quality in a Muslim-Majority Context
nonprofit.short_title: Muslim Students Trust in Government Institutions: The Role of Religiosity, Administrative Tran…
nonprofit.source: Journal of Government and Civil Society
nonprofit.plain_summary: Public trust in government institutions is crucial for effective governance, especially among educated youth in Muslim-majority societies. This study found that university students' trust in government is influenced by factors like religiosity, administrative transparency, and service quality. The research showed that service quality has the most significant impact on students' trust, more so than transparency or religious values. The study suggests that improving service quality is the most effective strategy for building trust in government institutions among young people.

nonprofit.title: Citizen Trust and Digital Governance Transformation: Ethical Challenges and Artificial Intelligence Governance in the Public Sector
nonprofit.short_title: Citizen Trust and Digital Governance Transformation: Ethical Challenges and Artificial Intelli…
nonprofit.source: Journal of Government and Civil Society
nonprofit.plain_summary: This study explores how public trust in AI-driven government services is growing, focusing on ethical considerations, explainable AI, and digital government transformation. It shows a rise in academic publications about these topics, indicating increasing interest in making AI more transparent and accountable. Key countries like the US, Germany, the UK, the Netherlands, and China are major contributors to this research. The findings highlight the importance of making AI understandable, ensuring ethical governance, and promoting transparency to build trust with citizens.

nonprofit.title: Corruption Network in Bank BJB Advertising Procurement: An NVivo Content Analysis
nonprofit.short_title: Corruption Network in Bank BJB Advertising Procurement: An NVivo Content Analysis
nonprofit.source: Journal of Government and Civil Society
nonprofit.plain_summary: This study examines corruption in the Bank BJB advertising procurement case, analyzing eight news reports from different media sources. The findings show that corruption was sustained through patronage, mutual benefit relationships, brokers, and informal networks. These practices led to financial losses for the state, policy distortions, reduced oversight, and declining accountability. The study highlights how actor configurations and relational mechanisms support organized corruption, offering insights for improving transparency and governance in public procurement.
